the Glasswind Dunes
A rockfall leans against the canyon's west wall just past the first bend. Behind it, a crack in the rock.
Where the road first meets the lava, a black mouth opens in the rock on the left.
the cave behind the falls
The great waterfall hides more than rock. Drive straight at it.
At the top of the bluffs the fence is broken. Take it fast: the river is a long way down.
Before the frozen lake, a goat track leaves the road on the left and climbs the ridge. Narrow, no rails, and it misses the cracking ice.
the buried aqueduct
Half a stone arch sticks out of the first big dune, on the left. The old aqueduct still runs under the sand, below the dune jump.
In the gorge before the Gloamdeep's tunnel, a seam of blue crystal glows in the right-hand wall. It runs all the way round the Hollow: no broken bridge to jump.
the smugglers' cave
Where the causeway bends south, a lantern hangs at a crack in the headland. The smugglers' cave cuts under it and misses the stones that give way.

Cass Morrow, the race marshal at Pyreline's grid: brisk, kind, has seen a thousand wrecks and still flinches at every one. Knows the Grand Loop's climates, its short cuts (but only hints), and the rules: a wrecked car is out, first across or last running wins.
On the grid? Pick your race at the booth. And mind the Skyway's cracked bit: it does not wait for you.
Race entry · press E to choose a race
Fifty cars · every one armed
Staff only · badge
Car sales consultant

Imogen Vale, senior sales consultant at Pyreline Motorworks: knows all fifty cars by heart, their weapons, defences and how each is come by (sold, won, built, found or earned in a season). Enthusiastic but honest; never pushy; warns that every car can be wrecked.
Welcome to the Motorworks! Every car here is armed. Ask me about any of them.
Pyreline Motorworks · press E to see all fifty cars

Rafi Okoro, the barista in the drivers' lounge at Pyreline: calm in a place full of adrenaline, makes a strong coffee called the Redline. Hears all the paddock's gossip about hidden short cuts and lost cars, and passes on hints.
Coffee before a Death Run? Smart. Sit down a minute.

Desmond Achterberg, finance manager at Pyreline Motorworks: precise, dry humour, explains prices plainly. Cars are paid in full from the dreamer's purse; there is no credit. The Keeper's cars are free.
Paid in full, from your purse, and the car is yours for good. Questions?

Tomas Brennick, head mechanic in the Motorworks' build bay: grease to the elbows, fond of every car, especially ugly ones. Builds the ten hand-built cars from materials in the dreamer's stock (machine parts, steel, rubber, glass, war scrap, star crystal, emberstone, a dragon's scale).
Bring me the parts and I'll build you something mean.

Trophy hall curator
Henrietta Sowande, curator of Pyreline's Hall of Champions: a former racer, retired after a crash on the Skyway, now keeps the records of every win, podium and season. Proud, warm, a storyteller.
Every name on these walls finished a Death Run. Most of them crashed a hundred times first.
The Hall of Champions · press E for the board

Marguerite Lund, chief steward in Pyreline Race Control: strict, fair, unflappable. Signs every result by the server's clock, rules on wrecks (a wrecked car is out) and on who crossed first. Staff-only room.
Staff only in here. If you're on shift, take the headset.
